newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka needs extra 3,000 MW power over 14 years.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka needs extra 3,000 MW power over 14 years.

text.p: Sri Lanka needs to boost its electricity supply by 3,000 MW to meet national demand over the next 14 years, a state-utility official said on Friday.
Demand for electricity in Sri Lanka is projected to grow by 10 percent annually, said D.G.D.C. Wijeratne, Deputy General Manager of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).
"We have to add another 1,000 MW for the period 1997-2005," he told Reuters. "And 2,000 MW will be needed on top of this for the period 2005-2012."
According to the Sri Lankan Ministry of Irrigation and Power, the country has a total electricity supply capacity of 1,785 MW, of which 1,115 MW is hydropower.
But a series of droughts in recent years has made hydropower a sometimes unreliable source of power and has led to island-wide shortages and power-cuts.
The CEB aims to increase Sri Lanka's thermal power supply to 670 MW by building a 300-MW coal-fired plant north of the capital Colombo.
Analysts say much of Sri Lanka's new power supply will probably come from oil-fired power stations, increasing the Indian Ocean island's dependency on diesel (gas oil) imports.
